method: Manual whole-file reading of four files, 877 lines; pinned Git bytes verified. Source review only.
findings: ArrangeChildren initializes output bounds/state and dispatches Rows, Squarified, Hilbert or Moore. Nonincreasing weights, trailing zeros and parent-weight sum are caller preconditions checked with assertions, not release input validation.

Rows and Squarified distribute all-zero inputs into equal vertical strips. Mixed zero weights and pixel rounding can yield degenerate rectangles, including for tiny positive weights; no minimum visible area guarantee.
Squarified computes rowThickness * rowThickness as integer multiplication before floating-point use; extremely large dimensions could overflow. No actual Windows viewport counterexample established.

Hilbert/Moore uses 14 patterns and average aspect ratio selection; contiguous four-way partitioning uses cumulative double weights and a variance heuristic. This is not proof of a globally optimal partition.

Unsigned 64-bit weights become doubles and cumulative sums: very small positive weights next to dominant weights can lose numerical distinction. All-zero curve weights become equal unit weights; mixed zeros are skipped.
Recursive partitions use Hilbert curves internally even for the outer Moore variant. Pixel conversion rounds and clamps to parent bounds.
HilbertMooreTreeMap.cpp includes an MIT attribution to the 2021 HPI Visual Analytics group. Nested licensing differs from repository-level GPL metadata; no code copied.
limits: No Windows application, layout runtime, rendering, performance or numeric-boundary tests executed for this increment.
